findings.statement: CXCR2 tops the convergence ranking: up in UC in all five cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.264], and higher in inflamed than non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient, paired log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=1.6972]. Caveat: CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor, so the bulk signal probably reflects neutrophil infiltration rather than a change inside the epithelium; clinical-stage antagonists exist (navarixin, reparixin, ladarixin).

CXCL8 (IL-8), the ligand of CXCR1 and CXCR2, is strongly and reproducibly up in all five cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=CXCL8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.7037]. It is a local inflammation marker (paired inflamed vs non-inflamed increase) but the source is mixed epithelial, myeloid and neutrophil.

OSMR (receptor for oncostatin M) is up in inflamed vs non-inflamed mucosa of the same patient, paired log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=0.8848], but nearly flat in non-inflamed mucosa vs control, log2FC [gene=OSMR; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.1755]. This pattern marks local inflammation, and the increase is replicated in all four microarray cohorts.

HMGCS2, an epithelial ketogenesis gene, is lost in inflamed mucosa, paired log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=-1.9508], and is unchanged in non-inflamed mucosa vs control, log2FC [gene=HMGCS2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=-0.0649]. It is down in all five cohorts. It is a marker of local inflammation and epithelial metabolic failure, not a drug target.

CHI3L1 has the largest reproducible increase among top-ranked genes, up in all five cohorts. It is much higher in inflamed than paired non-inflamed mucosa, log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=inflamed_vs_noninflamed_paired; log2fc=2.6182]. It is also modestly raised in non-inflamed mucosa, log2FC [gene=CHI3L1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE193677; layer=rna; cohort=GSE193677; contrast=noninflamed_vs_control; log2fc=0.8377], so it carries some disease-level signal as well as local inflammation. It has no genetic evidence and no drug.

JAK2 is a genetically supported, drug-tractable JAK-pathway node, but its expression change is modest, with pooled log2FC [gene=JAK2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=0.872]. The convergence rank comes from genetics, literature and tractability, not from a large expression change, so expression adds little discrimination for JAK2.

IDO1 (tryptophan catabolism) is up in all five cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=IDO1; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=3.445]. It is an interferon-response gene, and inhibitors exist (epacadostat, linrodostat). It has no genetic support in the ranking, and the bulk signal includes myeloid cells.

CD274 (PD-L1) is up in UC in all five cohorts, pooled log2FC [gene=CD274; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=1.887]. It indicates an interferon-driven counter-regulatory program. Its tractability comes from oncology checkpoint drugs, which would be inhibitors of a regulatory brake and so are not a rational UC strategy.

DUOX2 is one of the strongest epithelial up-regulated genes, pooled log2FC [gene=DUOX2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=4.3213], up in all five cohorts with a large paired inflamed vs non-inflamed increase. DUOXA2 and TNIP3 behave the same way. This is an epithelial innate stress program, a good local-inflammation biomarker with no drug and no genetic support.

REG1A is up in the MSCCR and the other cohorts, but in the Leuven infliximab cohort the increase is not significant, padj [gene=REG1A; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:GSE16879; layer=rna; cohort=GSE16879; contrast=uc_vs_control; padj=0.132]. Replication is therefore four of five cohorts, weaker than the top genes.

CLDN8, a tight-junction gene, is the most strongly lost gene in the meta-analysis, pooled log2FC [gene=CLDN8; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=-4.5181], down in all five cohorts. It reflects loss of epithelial barrier and absorptive identity, as with SLC26A2, AQP8, PCK1 and GUCA2A/B. These are biomarkers of mucosal damage, not targets.

caveats: Microarray fold changes are compressed relative to RNA-seq, so only direction and significance were compared across cohorts.
Immune and neutrophil genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8, S100A8/9, IL1B, CD274, IDO1) are confounded by infiltrating cells in inflamed mucosa; cell composition is not resolved here.
The non-inflamed vs control contrast comes only from MSCCR; the four microarray cohorts compare UC at baseline with healthy controls, so local vs disease-level changes are judged from MSCCR alone.
The paired inflamed vs non-inflamed comparison covers 135 patients in one cohort.
Heterogeneity across cohorts is high for most top genes, so pooled fold changes are approximate.
Genes with weak expression change but strong genetics or drugs (JAK2, FCGR2A, IL2RA) rank high because of non-expression streams.
